note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Decode load imbalance under unknown output lengths motivates predict-calibrate-schedule pipeline, evaluated end to end

nodes.name: Heavy-tailed output lengths
nodes.description: Real-world LLM workloads have highly skewed, heavy-tailed output length distributions, producing heterogeneous decoding demand and uneven KV cache consumption.

nodes.name: Decoder load imbalance
nodes.description: Identically provisioned decoders gradually diverge in KV cache utilization, with some persistently saturated while others stay underutilized.

nodes.name: Stateless routing fails
nodes.description: Round-robin routing fails to balance decoders and can worsen queue buildup and preemption; least-request treats request count as load proxy and saturates under long generations, so vLLM and SGLang keep RR.

nodes.name: Prior length-aware work is limited
nodes.description: PO-IT and Ranking only enable SJF within a single decode instance without cross-instance placement, prediction can add critical-path latency, and Llumnix migrates after imbalance occurs at significant overhead for large KV caches.

nodes.name: Device-assisted speculative prediction
nodes.description: A LoRA-fine-tuned lightweight LLM on the request-origin device predicts output length in parallel with cloud-side prefill, hiding prediction latency; its training target is the maximum output length across LLaMA and Qwen models under multiple temperatures.

nodes.name: Underestimation is the costly error
nodes.description: Underestimating output length triggers queue buildup, preemption and multi-fold latency inflation, whereas moderate overestimation only causes conservative allocation mitigated by PagedAttention.

nodes.name: Uncertainty-aware conformal calibration
nodes.description: UAC computes one-sided nonconformity scores over a sliding window of recent requests and sets the upper bound L_up = L_pred + q_alpha, guaranteeing P(L_out <= L_up) >= 1 - alpha under exchangeability.

nodes.name: Memory-aware global routing
nodes.description: The global scheduler estimates KV demand B = ceil((L_prompt + L_up)/S), keeps only decoders whose effective free blocks fit it, routes to the feasible decoder with the shortest waiting queue, and reserves blocks atomically; it falls back to RR on timeout and to maximum capacity if none is feasible.

nodes.name: Local SJF reordering
nodes.description: Because per-token latency is stable, decoding time is roughly proportional to output length, so each decoder reorders its queue by L_up (SJF) with a maximum waiting time to avoid starvation, mitigating head-of-line blocking.

nodes.name: Prediction accuracy
nodes.description: On Alpaca, SP-7B reduces MAE by 11.1% over PO-IT and 21.1% over S3, with higher Acc-50 and Acc-100.

nodes.name: Calibration lowers underestimation
nodes.description: UAC substantially lowers underestimation probability and caps residual error versus raw SP or a fixed 10% offset heuristic.

nodes.name: Main latency gains
nodes.description: Across ShareGPT and BurstGPT workloads and LLaMA3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-3B, MAPS cuts mean E2E latency by 42.6% and P99 E2E latency by up to 84.8% versus vLLM, SGLang and Llumnix.

nodes.name: Better balance
nodes.description: At high load MAPS keeps the decoders' queue-length ratio at 0.96 versus 1.36x under vLLM, with queues reduced on both decoders.

nodes.name: Robust to weak predictor
nodes.description: MAPS-160M still beats all baselines (E2E P99 improved 21.5%/21.0%/56.8% over SGLang/vLLM/Llumnix) and MAPS stays within 19.8% of the oracle's P99, so limited headroom remains for predictor improvement.

nodes.name: Ablation: UAC
nodes.description: Removing UAC raises P99 and mean E2E latency by 14.3% and 18.4% because underestimation causes preemption and cascading queue delays.

nodes.name: Ablation: routing policy
nodes.description: Replacing minimum-queue routing with maximum-capacity routing degrades latency (Qwen2.5-3B P99 and mean up to 1.11x and 1.36x), showing routing should target queue buildup rather than residual memory.

nodes.name: Ablation: SJF
nodes.description: Replacing local SJF with FCFS consistently increases mean and tail latency, more at P99 under higher rates.

isolated_nodes.name: Runtime state collection
isolated_nodes.description: Each decoder's monitor periodically reports free, reserved and effective blocks and queue length to a Redis-backed runtime state collector that also holds a sliding window of recent outcomes.

isolated_nodes.name: Tail latency vs baselines
isolated_nodes.description: Llumnix shows large max inter-token latency due to migration under memory pressure, while vLLM and SGLang show rapid TTFT growth under load and MAPS keeps max ITL low and stable.

isolated_nodes.name: Limitations
isolated_nodes.description: Evaluation uses only six A6000 GPUs (one prefiller, two decoders), predictor is fine-tuned on Alpaca and may need adaptation for other workloads, and chain-of-thought length prediction remains open.

structural_reasoning: Argument flows from the load-imbalance problem and prior-work gaps to prediction, calibration and hierarchical scheduling, then to evaluation and ablations.
